input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: Async wrapper clears and reuses a single shared statistics dict for all concurrent invocations.
- rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather of several calls to the same decorated coroutine function. Each call does stats.clear() and writes into the same dict, so stats from in-flight calls are reset and mixed. Impact: wrong attempt_number and start times, which affects wait and stop decisions that read statistics.
critique: Both describe the same fault: a single statistics dict is cleared and reused across calls. Concurrent calls to the decorated function wipe and mix each other's start_time and attempt_number. The finding uses the async gather case, which the label explicitly covers.
